questions.statement: It is 8:00. How do you say this?
questions.context: Learning about telling the time in English class.

options.feedback: 8:00 is spoken as 'It is eight o'clock', because the minutes are zero.
8:00 has no minutes to name, so nothing is said after 'eight'.
You do not say the time in hours like that; the hour is named once, as 'eight'.
Seconds are far too small a unit to describe a whole hour.

The short (hour) hand shows the hours; the long hand is the one that shows minutes.
Days are counted by the calendar, not read off a clock face.
